text:
Sam R.: Heads up — acme-corp opened an escalation: p99 for their /chat route jumped from ~450ms to ~3.2s this morning and they reported intermittent CUDA OOMs on the dedicated GPU pool. Ticket: #12345. One request id: req_9a8b7c. Partial logs attached in the ticket.

Lia M.: Which model/version are they on? Is it constant or spikes only on long contexts?

Sam R.: Model is gpt-neo-4b-quant (runtime v2.3.1). Sequence lengths often ~1.2k-1.8k tokens (multi-turn chat). Appears correlated with long-lived sessions. Some requests OOM, others just p99 slow without OOM.

Alex P.: Did we change any KV/cache config or allocator around the v2.3.1 rollout? I recall we toggled the new allocator mode yesterday.

deploy-bot: deploy runtime-dedicated v2.3.1 -> runtime-dedicated pool completed (2026-03-14T03:22Z)

Mike (oncall): I pulled logs for req_9a8b7c. Seeing cuMemAlloc failed stack and a bunch of large KV tensor refs. Snippet:

```
2026-03-14 05:12:11,532 ERROR runtime.worker: OutOfMemoryError: cuMemAlloc failed (requested 201326592)
  File "/app/runtime/serving.py", line 421, in handle_request
    kv_store.append(new_kv)
  ...
```

Mike (oncall): Also seeing a couple of workers where there's no OOM but p99 ~2.6s and GPU mem shows lots of allocated blocks with holes (fragmentation). nvidia-smi snapshot:

```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| GPU  Name       Persistence-M| Bus-Id        Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr. ECC |
| 0    Tesla T4         Off   | 00000000:00:1E.0 Off |                    0 |
| Fan  Temp  Perf  Pwr:Usage/Cap|   Memory-Usage | GPU-Util |
|      45C    P0    34W /  70W  |  14887MiB / 16384MiB |    72%   |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
Processes:  
|   3123 python3  14887MiB |
```

Lia M.: That points at KV cache growth + allocator not returning memory to CUDA. Two immediate mitigations we can try:
- throttle concurrency for acme-corp route (reduce simultaneous contexts)
- route them to a smaller model temporarily (gpt-neo-2b-quant)
- set a hard cap on per-session KV entries

Sam R.: Customer prefers a gateway-side fix (no app changes). I can add a route override to send them to 2b for now. Would prefer we avoid frequent restarts.

Alex P.: Long-term root cause: KV cache growth + fragmentation due to our allocator's caching behavior. Yesterday's allocator toggle (tcmalloc-ish mode) can retain device memory leading to fragmentation if KV entries are churny. Quick config to test: set KV_MAX_ENTRIES=200000 and KV_PRUNE_STRATEGY=LRU on runtime pods, and try ALLOCATOR_MODE=compact to force the allocator to return freed blocks sooner.

Sam R.: Can we roll that config to a small canary this morning?

deploy-bot: kubectl set env deploy/runtime-worker -n runtime KV_MAX_ENTRIES=200000 KV_PRUNE_STRATEGY=LRU --record

Mike (oncall): Did a rolling restart of 6 workers in the affected pool after env change. Observed p99 drop to ~600ms for ~20 minutes then creep back up slowly.

Lia M.: That suggests the eviction helps short-term but fragmentation accumulates over time. We should also add a periodic KV compaction job and an explicit GPU memory compaction path when pruning large KV tensors.

Mike (oncall): Also adding alerting: if gpu_free_frag_ratio > 0.35 && p99_latency > 1s for 5m -> page oncall and reduce traffic for that pool. I'll wire that into the runtime dashboard.

Sam R.: Customer routed to 2b for now. I'll send a customer note: temporary mitigation applied, expected timeline for config changes 72h, deeper allocator fix in 2 weeks.

CS Bot: Ticket #12345 updated: mitigation applied (route override -> gpt-neo-2b-quant). Next update scheduled in 24h.

Alex P.: Action items and owners:
- Lia M. -> PR to add per-route KV hard caps + prune-strategy defaults (ETA 72h)
- Mike (oncall) -> dashboard + alert (ETA 24h)
- Alex P. -> allocator investigation & prototype compact-mode changes (ETA 2 weeks)
- Sam R. -> customer comms & interim routing (ongoing)

Lia M.: Also noting: benchmark the perf delta for ALLOCATOR_MODE=compact vs default. It may slightly increase average latency but improve p99 stability. We'll run perf tests in staging.

Sam R.: Thanks team. I'll keep this thread updated with customer feedback. If anyone finds a clear repro we can run a targeted job to validate fixes.

Alex P.: One more note — add a periodic process restart as a temporary band-aid for long-lived workers (cron restart every 12h) while we ship compaction, to keep fragmentation low. Not ideal but buy time.

Mike (oncall): I'll coordinate the cron restart for canary workers and monitor.

Sam R.: Good. Closing loop for now. Updates as they come. :thumbsup:
